preamble: Merger of the glottalized postalveolar fricative with the glottalized alveolar affricate in Kansa (Kaw), a Dhegihan Siouan language; Osage shows the same reflex. The Comparative Siouan Dictionary (CSD) reconstructs Proto-Mississippi Valley and Proto-Dhegiha *šʔ, the series that Wikipedia's table of Proto-Siouan consonants gives as ejective *ʃʼ. Quapaw keeps it as /ʃʼ/, and Omaha-Ponca also keeps šʔ (Omaha-Ponca įšʔáge 'old man', Quapaw šʔaké hí 'elder, an old man'), while Kansa and Osage have cʔ. In Rankin's transcription c is the alveolar affricate, and cʔ is the /tsʼ/ of both languages: Kansa has /tsʼ/ and no glottalized fricatives (Kaw orthography ts', as in ts'e 'dead'; CSD set 'die': Kanza čʔé, bücʔé), and Osage has a single dental-alveolar ejective that is always fricated (Wikipedia's Osage article writes cʼéðe [tsʼɛˑðɛ] 'he killed it'; cf. La Flesche's ṭs’éthe in the CSD set 'kill (2)', where the CSD normalizes La Flesche's ṭs’ as cʔ). Proto-Dhegiha *sʔ has the same reflex (*sʔáre 'sour' > Kanza cʔáye; *wésʔa 'hiss' > Kanza and Osage wécʔa; *okásʔį 'peek' > Kanza ogácʔį), so both glottalized sibilants merged as /tsʼ/. Rankin, Carter & Jones (1998) state that glottalized fricatives are found only in Mississippi Valley Siouan, so the source value is a Mississippi Valley and Proto-Dhegiha reconstruction, not an attested stage. The CSD gives no prose statement of the change; it rests on the cognate sets below. Because *sʔ also gives cʔ, only sets whose šʔ is confirmed by a sister language show the change: 'old man' (Omaha-Ponca, Quapaw) and 'feeble' (Lakota). In 'drip' the CSD also has an *sʔe grade of the root, and Quapaw varies between šʔ, tsʔ and čʔ, so that set does not show which grade Kansa and Osage continue.

examples.note: CSD 'old man', source Rankin. Omaha-Ponca įšʔáge 'old man' and Quapaw šʔaké hí 'elder, an old man' keep šʔ. Osage has the same reflex as Kansa: iṭs’age, CSD †icʔáge 'little old man, sister-in-law's father' (La Flesche, LF:80b). The CSD entry 'brave (1)' lists the Kansa word as cʔágehįga 'a tribal elder' under Proto-Dhegiha *šʔáke.

CSD 'feeble', source Rankin; no Proto-Dhegiha form is given. Lakota keeps šʔ in the same compound: -šʔákA, ya- 'make no impression with the mouth'. The CSD cross-refers 'fail' (Proto-Dhegiha *šʔa; Quapaw šʔá, di- 'fail, fall short').

CSD 'drip (3)', source Rankin; Osage ágaṭs’e, CSD †ákacʔe 'drop water on' (LF:8b). Not decisive: the CSD also has an *sʔe grade ('drip (1)'), and Quapaw in this set has ditsʔétsʔe 'drip' and akačʔéčʔe 'drip onto' beside bišʔé 'scrub, bear down washing'.
